content: Insulin should be injected into subcutaneous tissue rather than intramuscularly. Injecting insulin into muscle tissue can lead to unpredictable absorption rates due to muscle activity, which may result in erratic blood glucose control. The recommended injection sites for subcutaneous insulin administration include the abdomen, thighs, buttocks, and upper arms. These areas are preferred because they provide consistent absorption when used correctly. Rotating injection sites is essential to prevent the development of lipohypertrophy. Lipohypertrophy refers to the formation of raised, hardened areas of fatty tissue caused by repeated injections in the same location. This condition can interfere with insulin absorption, leading to inconsistent glucose control. Educational training should emphasize proper site rotation techniques and the selection of appropriate needle lengths.
